_meta.indication: Ferriprox (deferiprone) is an iron chelator indicated for the treatment of patients with transfusional iron overload due to thalassemia syndromes when current chelation therapy is inadequate.

pivotal_trials.phase: Not specified; a prospective, planned, pooled analysis of existing study data
pivotal_trials.design: Single-arm, non-randomized, baseline-controlled pooled analysis of 12 previously conducted studies; patients selected by an Independent Party/Committee by pre-specified criteria.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with transfusional iron overload (almost all with thalassemia) who had been inadequately treated with other iron chelators (mostly deferoxamine); main chelation-failure criterion serum ferritin >2,500 mcg/L.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: change in serum ferritin from baseline to within one year of therapy; success defined as a ≥20% decline in serum ferritin, with trial deemed effective if ≥20% of patients achieved it.
pivotal_trials.n: 264 patients eligible for the primary serum ferritin efficacy analysis
pivotal_trials.result: Overall success rate for serum ferritin was 52% (95% CI 45%, 58%); 136 (52%) of patients had a ≥20% decrease in serum ferritin; lower CI limit >20% so endpoint met.

key_safety: Most serious adverse reaction is agranulocytosis (1.7% of patients in pooled trials). Most common adverse reactions (≥5%) are chromaturia (14.6%), nausea (12.6%), abdominal pain/discomfort (10.4%), vomiting (9.8%), arthralgia (9.8%), ALT increased (7.5%) and neutropenia (6.2%).
target_moa: Deferiprone is a synthetic, orally active iron-chelating agent with affinity for ferric ion (iron III); it binds ferric ions to form stable 3:1 (deferiprone:iron) complexes that are excreted, with lower affinity for other metals.

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: AGRANULOCYTOSIS/NEUTROPENIA — Ferriprox can cause agranulocytosis that can lead to serious infections and death; neutropenia may precede agranulocytosis. Measure ANC before starting and monitor weekly on therapy.

advisory_committee.vote: Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee met September 14, 2011 and voted 10 (yes) to 2 (no) that the available clinical data demonstrate a favorable risk-benefit profile for deferiprone.

Success for a particular patient will be declared if there is a decrease in serum ferritin of at least 20% compared to baseline. Success for the entire study will be declared if a successful outcome is observed in at least 20% of treated patients
